findings_qualitative.value: G0.02 is part of an elliptical structure in the longitude-velocity diagram (the mini-CMZ) corresponding to an inclined 10-pc ring rotating at ~104 km s^-1 with ~100 km s^-1 noncircular motion.

evidence.quote: The entire ellipse is geometrically equivalent to an LV feature that represents a ring of radius R = 9.3 pc, which rotates at A = 104 km s^{-1} and expands at B = 100 km s^{-1} .

We showed that G0.02 is an edge-on view of a part of a molecular ring of radius _∼_ 10 pc rotating around Sgr A _[∗]_ in _V_ rot _∼_ 100 km s _[−]_ [1] superposed by noncircular motion of _∼_ 100 km s _[−]_ [1] .

findings_qualitative.value: The sky morphology, arc-shaped LVD, and broad lopsided line profile of G0.02 are reproduced by an eccentric orbit of gas flowing in the gravitational potential of an extended mass distribution, with velocity width driven by orbital shear near the tangential point.

evidence.loc: 3.3.5 Eccentric motion in a spherical potential (U -type) - Panel F, G -
evidence.quote: However, if we cut part of the orbit as in panel G, it reproduces the observed properties such as the curved arc near the tangential direction, the arc-shaped PVD, and the broad line profile that increases toward the sharp end.
Because G0.02 is located near the tangential direction of this ellipse, the width of the molecular line increases to several tens km s^{-1} due to shear in orbital velocity.

findings_qualitative.value: A compact bound cloud of radius ~1.6 pc and mass ~10^5 M_sun is tidally disrupted within one orbit in the central 10 pc bulge potential, supporting the view that G0.02 is agalactic arm or density wave feature rather than an isolated cloud.

evidence.quote: The cloud is strongly stretched to make a spiral shape and loses its identity within one orbital rotation. Since such a compact cloud can easily be disrupted, it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc.

claims.hypothesis: The anomalous high-velocity kinematics, elliptical LVD, and broad lopsided line width of G0.02 are caused by orbital shear in an eccentric gas flow within the central extended-mass gravitational potential rather than solely a local supernova explosion.
claims.experiment: Analyze ACES CS (J=2-1) moment 0 maps, LVDs, and line profiles of the central 10 pc (mini-CMZ) and compare them with N-particle orbital simulations in spherical, disc, and bar potentials as well as SN-driven shell and expanding ring models.
claims.result: The LV ridges trace a tilted ellipse (R = 9.3 pc, V_rot = 104 km s^-1, V_exp = 100 km s^-1); test-particle simulations of eccentric orbits in an extended potential reproduce the curved sky arc, U-type PVD, and broad (2*sigma_v ~ 56 km s^-1) lopsided line profile, while the high-velocity wing and O-type global LVD are better matched by SN expansion and expanding-ring models respectively.
claims.finding: G0.02 is well explained as a kinematic tracer of eccentric orbital motion in the nuclear gravitational potential, though expanding-ring and local SN expansion contributions cannot be ruled out.

evidence.quote: The projected shape in the sky and the global elliptical LVD of G0.02 are generally explained by the eccentric orbit model in the gravitational potential due to an extended mass distribution. However, the O -type LV feature is better reproduced by the expanding-ring model, and the high-velocity LV wing is explained by the SN-induced local expansion model. So, we cannot rule out these models at this time.

Because G0.02 is located near the tangential direction of this ellipse, the width of the molecular line increases to several tens km s^{-1} due to shear in orbital velocity. G+0.02-0.02+100 is thus a kinematic tracer of the inner potential, a rare case of a dense gas following an eccentric orbit in the nuclear gravitational field.

claims.hypothesis: G0.02 is part of a rotating circumnuclear disc arm or density wave rather than a self-gravitating compact molecular cloud.
claims.experiment: Calculate the virial mass and Roche radius of G0.02 and simulate the orbital evolution of a test-particle cloud bound by a local Plummer potential (m_c ~ 10^5 M_sun, r_c ~ 1.6 pc) inside the central bulge potential (M_B ~ 2.5 x 10^7 M_sun within 10 pc).
claims.result: M_vir (~4 x 10^5 M_sun) exceeds the molecular mass (~10^5 M_sun), and the simulated Plummer cloud is stretched into a spiral and tidally disrupted within one orbital period; the sky ellipse tilt (i_hat ~ 16 deg, PA ~ 74 deg) also aligns with Arm V and the CND.
claims.finding: Molecular clouds can hardly survive tidal disruption in the central 10 pc, so G0.02 is more naturally understood as an arm or wave in a tilted 10-pc circumnuclear ring.

evidence.loc: Section 4.3.1 Tidal disruption of a cloud
evidence.quote: it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc. Therefore, it is more natural to consider that G0.02 is a part of the rotating disc as an arm or a wave

The cloud is strongly stretched to make a spiral shape and loses its identity within one orbital rotation. Since such a compact cloud can easily be disrupted, it is generally difficult for any molecular cloud to survive disruption in the central 10 pc. Therefore, it is more natural to consider that G0.02 is a part of the rotating disc as an arm or a wave orbiting around the potential of the central bulge.

why_this_data.value: ACES provides high-resolution 12m+7m+TP cubes across the CMZ; CS (J=2-1) was chosen over H13CN (J=1-0) because CS (J=2-1) covers -220 <= v_LSR <= 220 km s^-1 whereas the H13CN internal release cube only covered -200 <= v_LSR <= 200 km s^-1, which was insufficient for G0.02.

evidence.quote: We also have the H^{13}CN (J = 1 - 0) line at 86.3399 GHz, but the velocity coverage (-200 \le v_LSR \le 200 km s^{-1} ) in the current internal release data was not sufficient for the purpose of this paper to explore G0.02. So, we restricted our analysis to the CS (J = 2 - 1 ) line that covers -220 \le v_LSR \le 220 km s^{-1} .

why_this_method.value: Test-particle orbital simulations in analytical gravitational potentials allow exploration of overall 3D orbital trajectories, PVD morphologies, and velocity shear line profiles across spherical, disc, and bar potentials.

evidence.loc: 3.2 Non-circular motion in the extended-mass potential
evidence.quote: In order to explain these kinematical properties, we simulate the evolution of a molecular cloud orbiting in the gravitational potential in the central stellar bulge.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Circularly rotating ring in a spherical potential (I-type PVD): rejected as unrealistic because it requires hydrostatic equilibrium in the radial direction and only produces a straight I-type ridge.

evidence.loc: 3.3.2 Rotating ring in spherical potential (I -type) - Panel B (figure 3) -
evidence.quote: However, such a circular rotation is realized only if the gas disc is in hydrostatic equilibrium in the radial direction, which may not be realistic here.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SN-induced local expanding shell: explains the large velocity width and high-velocity straight LV wing, but predicts a symmetric line profile rather than the observed lopsided profile and requires large energy injection (~10^52 erg); not ruled out for the high-velocity wing.

evidence.loc: 3.3.3 SN-induced local expanding cloud - Panel C -
evidence.quote: The result explains the large velocity width, but the line profile is symmetric with respect to the systemic velocity.
However, the high-velocity LV wing seems better explained by the SN expansion model but it predicts a more symmetric profile and requires large-energy injection.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Expanding ring in a spherical potential (O-type PVD) driven by nuclear activity / focusing MHD wave: reproduces the global O-type LVD of the mini-CMZ and cannot be ruled out.

evidence.loc: 3.3.4 Expanding ring in a spherical potential (O -type) - Panel D, E -
evidence.quote: This model well reproduces the O -type LVD observed in the mini-CMZ shown in panel A.

However, the O -type LV feature is better reproduced by the expanding-ring model, and the high-velocity LV wing is explained by the SN-induced local expansion model. So, we cannot rule out these models at this time.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Eccentric flow in a flat disc (q = 1:1:0.63) or triaxial bar potential (q = 1:0.85:0.63): considered and found to produce similar U-type / II-type LVDs and lopsided line profiles that can also explain G0.02.

evidence.loc: 3.3.6 Non-circular flow in disc and bar potentials (U, II -type) - Panel H, I -
evidence.quote: The LVD behaviors are similar to that in the spherical potential (panel F), and a part of LVD may explain the LVD of G0.02.

limitations_admitted.value: Test-particle simulations neglect hydrodynamic, MHD, and nuclear feedback effects (except in the expanding ring model) and do not perform resonance analysis for closed orbits.

evidence.loc: 3.2 Non-circular motion in the extended-mass potential
evidence.quote: The integration was performed for a given initial condition without resonance analysis, so that the motion does not necessarily realize closed resonant orbits. In the test particle simulations here, the hydrodynamic and MHD effects are not evaluated, so the results apply only to the overall orbital behavior in the gravitational potential.

limitations_admitted.value: Solving the initial value problem for test particles does not uniquely rule out alternative models (such as expanding ring or local SN expansion).

evidence.loc: 3.2 Non-circular motion in the extended-mass potential
evidence.quote: The general agreement is that solving the initial value problem does not rule out other models, including those concluded here as unlikely.

limitations_admitted.value: The eccentric orbit simulation reproduces the general properties of G0.02 except for the high-velocity straight LV wing.

evidence.quote: The general property is well reproduced except for the high velocity straight LV wing.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ellipse fit to the LVD (Eq. 1) is done by eye/manual reading of ridge positions rather than an objective statistical fit with parameter uncertainties.
The test-particle simulations are dimensionless and matched qualitatively to the data without quantitative optimization of physical scales or viewing angles.
Collisional and hydrodynamic shocks at high orbital eccentricity in the inner 10 pc could strongly alter gas trajectories compared to ballistic test particles.

data_public_as_stated.value: Internal release version of the ACES Large Program (2021.1.00172.L) data was used.

evidence.quote: The interferometer data were taken from the internal release version of the 12m+7m+TP (Total Power)-mode data from the ALMA cycle 8 Large Program "ALMA Central Molecular Zone Exploration Survey" (ACES, 2021.1.00172.L).

missing_for_reproduction: Public release of the combined 12m+7m+TP ACES CS (J=2-1) and H13CN (J=1-0) data cubes (paper uses an internal team release)
Exact background-subtraction procedure for removing horizontally extended LV components in Figure 2 and Figure 3A-b
Exact coordinates/aperture used to extract the G0.02 spectrum in Figure 3A-d and measure r ~ 0.7 pc
Test-particle simulation code, time-stepping details, and projection viewing angles used to generate Figures 2, 3, and 4
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB for the full ACES CS (J=2-1) combined cube; ~1-2 GB for the central cutout (-0.25 <= l <= +0.15 deg, -0.1 <= b <= 0.0 deg).
reproducibility.score_reason: The observational analysis (moment 0, maximum-intensity LVD, analytic ellipse equation) and the analytical equations for the test-particle potentials and initial conditions are explicitly given, but the data come from an internal ACES release, no software is named, the background LVD subtraction method is unspecified, and the ellipse fit and simulation comparisons are manual/qualitative.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper relies on an internal team data release of the combined 12m+7m+TP ACES cubes rather than publicly released archival cubes, and the primary analysis relies on manual reading of LVD ridges and qualitative test-particle comparisons.

methods_papers.why: Logarithmic potential formulation for triaxial bar and spherical mass distributions used in the test-particle simulations.

companion_papers.why: Paper I identifying Galactic-Center Arms I to VI in the CMZ and describing the ACES cubes used in this work.
Overview paper for the ALMA CMZ Exploration Survey (ACES) Large Program.
